import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_4.csv"

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
source3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
source4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']

# Step 1: Aggregate each source by 'batsman' with appropriate aggregation

# source0: sum batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x
agg_source0 = source0.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({'batsman_runs': 'sum'}).rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_x'})

# source2: sum batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y
agg_source2 = source2.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({'batsman_runs': 'sum'}).rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_y'})

# source3: sum batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y_6
agg_source3 = source3.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({'batsman_runs': 'sum'}).rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_y_6'})

# source4: rename batsman_runs to batsman_runs_x_4, aggregate sum for runs and balls, mean for strike
source4_renamed = source4.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_x_4'})
agg_source4 = source4_renamed.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({
    'batsman_runs_x_4': 'sum',
    'no of balls': 'sum',
    'strike': 'mean'
})

# source1: sum total_runs
agg_source1 = source1.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({'total_runs': 'sum'})

# Step 2: Merge all aggregated tables on 'batsman' using inner joins to keep only common batsmen
df = agg_source0
df = pd.merge(df, agg_source2, on='batsman', how='inner')
df = pd.merge(df, agg_source3, on='batsman', how='inner')
df = pd.merge(df, agg_source4, on='batsman', how='inner')
df = pd.merge(df, agg_source1, on='batsman', how='inner')

# Step 3: Fill NaN values with 0 or 0.0 (should not be needed after inner join, but safe)
int_cols = ['batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y', 'batsman_runs_y_6', 'batsman_runs_x_4', 'no of balls', 'total_runs']
for col in int_cols:
    df[col] = df[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

df['strike'] = df['strike'].fillna(0.0).astype(float)

# Step 4: Group by 'batsman' to ensure uniqueness and aggregate sums/mean (in case of duplicates)
df = df.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({
    'batsman_runs_x': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_y': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_y_6': 'sum',
    'batsman_runs_x_4': 'sum',
    'no of balls': 'sum',
    'strike': 'mean',
    'total_runs': 'sum'
})

# Step 5: Ensure data types again after groupby
for col in int_cols:
    df[col] = df[col].astype(int)
df['strike'] = df['strike'].astype(float)

# Step 6: Reorder columns to match target schema
target_columns = ['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_x_4', 'strike', 'batsman_runs_y_6', 'total_runs']
df = df[target_columns]

# Step 7: Save to output path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
